title: LETTER 13: Letter to Editor — Cyber Fraud and Banking Security

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Letters to the Editor must strictly adhere to the formal letter format: Sender's Address, Date, Receiver's Address, Subject, Salutation, Body, and Complimentary Close.
The subject line must be concise and clearly communicate the core topic, such as 'Rising Cyber Fraud and Urgent Need for Enhanced Banking Security'.
The body should be divided into three distinct paragraphs: introducing the issue, detailing its impact on citizens, and suggesting remedies.
Avoid requesting the Editor to solve the problem directly; instead, urge them to publish the letter to alert authorities and inform the public.

blocks.content: Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper, I wish to draw the attention of the authorities and the general public towards the alarming rise in cyber fraud and the urgent need for robust banking security.

rows: Manipulating users into revealing OTPs, PINs, or clicking malicious links
Fraudulently procuring a duplicate SIM card to intercept security OTPs
No (Fraudster operates directly through telecom service provider bypass)
Never share financial credentials and verify genuine banking channels
Immediately report unexpected mobile network disconnection to the operator

items: Do not write 'To' above 'The Editor' as modern formal letter layouts omit it.
Unless specified in the exam prompt, use fictitious credentials like 'XYZ, ABC Road' to avoid disclosing personal identity.
Focus on standard solutions such as two-factor authentication, digital literacy, and stringent penal measures under the IT Act.
